chapters.summary: Before ascending to heaven, Jesus promises the coming of the Holy Spirit; the disciples wait in prayer and choose Matthias to complete the number of the twelve apostles.
keyPoints: Jesus charges the disciples to wait in Jerusalem for the Father's promise, the Holy Spirit, who will clothe them with power to be his witnesses.
Jesus ascends from the Mount of Olives, and an angel promises that he will come again in like manner, filling the disciples with joy.
The disciples continue with one accord in prayer, and cast lots to choose Matthias to take Judas' place among the twelve.
chapters.application: Like the first disciples, let us pray earnestly and wait for the Holy Spirit's power, boldly bearing witness to the risen Lord to the uttermost part of the earth.

chapters.summary: The Holy Spirit descends at Pentecost; Peter's sermon leads three thousand to repent and turn to the Lord, and the church begins to be built up.
keyPoints: The Holy Spirit descends like tongues of fire, filling the disciples, who begin to speak in other tongues.
Peter quotes the prophet Joel and bears witness to the resurrection and ascension of Jesus.
The people are pricked in their hearts, are baptized into the Lord, and continue steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine.
chapters.application: May we be filled with the Holy Spirit and boldly proclaim the risen Christ, fellowshipping with one another in love and living out our witness.

chapters.summary: At the temple gate called Beautiful, Peter and John heal a lame man in the name of Jesus, and use the occasion to testify that Jesus is the Christ appointed by God, calling the people to repent and turn to him.
keyPoints: As Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, they meet a lame beggar at the gate called Beautiful.
Peter, in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, commands the lame man to rise up and walk.
Peter preaches to the people, proving that Jesus is the Christ, and urges them to repent, that their sins may be blotted out.
chapters.application: Let us act by faith in the name of Jesus, seize every opportunity to testify of the Lord's power to others, and keep a heart of repentance so we may receive renewal and blessing from God.

chapters.summary: Peter and John are questioned for healing the lame man; they boldly testify to Jesus' resurrection, and the church prays with one accord and holds all things in common.
keyPoints: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Peter declares that Jesus is the stone rejected by the builders, and that salvation is found in no other.
The rulers see the boldness of Peter and John, and seeing the healed man standing there, they have nothing to say against it.
The church prays together, the place is shaken, the believers are filled with the Holy Spirit, and they hold all things in common, distributing as anyone has need.
chapters.application: When we face persecution, let us ask the Lord for boldness to proclaim the gospel without fear; let the church be of one accord, sharing with one another and displaying the love of Christ.

chapters.summary: Ananias and Sapphira die for lying to the Holy Spirit; the apostles perform signs and wonders, and though persecuted, they continue to preach boldly.
keyPoints: Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Holy Spirit and fall down dead, filling the church with fear.
The apostles perform many signs and wonders, and more and more believe and are added to the Lord.
The apostles are persecuted by the council, but choose to obey God rather than men, and are delivered by the Lord's angel.
themes: Honesty and the Fear of God
chapters.application: Let us be honest and without pretense before God, obeying him rather than men, and rejoice even in suffering, counted worthy to bear his name.

chapters.summary: The early church appoints seven deacons to oversee the daily distribution; Stephen, full of grace and power, is falsely accused and arrested.
keyPoints: As the number of disciples grows, a complaint arises between the Grecians and the Hebrews over neglect in the daily ministration, so the apostles decide to appoint deacons to oversee it.
The church chooses Stephen and six others, men of good report and full of the Holy Spirit, and the apostles pray and lay hands on them.
Stephen does great wonders, and when his opponents cannot resist him, they hire men to falsely accuse him of blasphemy against Moses and against God.
chapters.application: When the church's work increases, let us learn to share the load and each serve in our own calling. When we face false accusation, let us rely on the Holy Spirit and hold fast to our faith, for the Lord will surely watch over us.

chapters.summary: Before the council, Stephen recounts the history of Israel, charges the people with resisting the Holy Spirit, and is finally stoned to death.
keyPoints: Stephen reviews God's dealings with Abraham, Joseph, and Moses, showing God's guiding hand throughout history.
He charges the people of Israel with rebelling against God, worshiping idols, killing the prophets, and even resisting the Holy Spirit.
Stephen sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at God's right hand, and is cast out of the city and stoned to death.
chapters.application: May we keep a spirit of obedience, never resisting the Holy Spirit's leading, and look to Jesus even in persecution, following Stephen's example of forgiveness.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the persecution that scatters the church after Stephen's martyrdom, as believers preach wherever they go; Philip proclaims the gospel in Samaria and to the Ethiopian eunuch, showing the gospel's wide advance.
keyPoints: Saul persecutes the church, scattering the believers to preach in every place, and Philip goes down to the city of Samaria to preach Christ.
In the wilderness, Philip meets the Ethiopian eunuch, explains the book of Isaiah to him, and baptizes him.
The Holy Spirit guides Philip's ministry; the eunuch believes and is baptized, and Philip is caught away to Azotus, where he continues preaching.
chapters.application: Even in hard circumstances, the gospel still advances. May we obey the Holy Spirit's leading, ready at any time to share the Lord's grace with those around us and bear witness to the joy of salvation.

chapters.summary: On the road to Damascus, Saul meets the risen Lord, repents and turns to him, becoming Paul the apostle who will carry the gospel to the Gentiles.
keyPoints: On the road, Saul is struck down by a great light, hears the Lord's voice, and is struck blind.
Ananias obeys the Lord's instruction and lays hands on Saul, whose sight is restored and who is baptized.
Saul preaches boldly in Damascus and Jerusalem, and escapes when the Jews plot to kill him.
chapters.application: Whatever our past, God can change us. When he calls, let us obey like Ananias, and proclaim the gospel boldly like Paul.

chapters.summary: After seeing a vision, Peter goes to Cornelius' house to preach the gospel; the Holy Spirit falls upon the Gentiles, and the church receives Gentile believers.
keyPoints: Cornelius prays devoutly, and an angel instructs him to send for Peter.
Peter sees a vision and understands that God is no respecter of persons, breaking down the boundary between clean and unclean.
As Peter preaches, the Holy Spirit falls, the Gentiles are baptized, and the church receives them.
chapters.application: God is no respecter of persons; his salvation comes to all people. Let us set aside prejudice, obey the Holy Spirit, and share the gospel with people of every background, bearing witness to God's love.

chapters.summary: Peter explains to the Jerusalem church how the Gentile Cornelius and his household came to believe; the church receives the Gentile believers, and the gospel begins to spread to non-Jews.
keyPoints: Peter recounts the vision and the coming of the Holy Spirit, proving that God has received the Gentiles.
Hearing Peter's testimony, the believers in Jerusalem glorify God, acknowledging that the Gentiles too have obtained salvation.
The church at Antioch is established, the disciples are first called Christians there, and Barnabas and Saul teach among them.
chapters.application: When God's work goes beyond our expectations and traditions, let us listen humbly to the testimony given, receive with an open heart what God has cleansed, and bear witness to the gospel in unity.

chapters.summary: This chapter records King Herod's persecution of the church, the killing of James, Peter's imprisonment and rescue by an angel, Herod's death for his pride, and the word of God continuing to grow and prevail.
keyPoints: Herod stretches out his hand to afflict the church, kills James with the sword, and imprisons Peter, while the church prays earnestly to God.
An angel delivers Peter from prison by night; Peter realizes it is the Lord's doing and goes to Mary's house, where the believers are gathered.
Herod fails to give God the glory and is eaten of worms and dies, but the word of God continues to grow and spread.
chapters.application: In the face of persecution, let us pray earnestly as the early church did, trusting God's deliverance; and let us guard against pride, giving glory to God, for he surely watches over his church.

chapters.summary: Sent by the Holy Spirit, Paul and Barnabas begin their first missionary journey, preaching the gospel in various places, and sharply rebuking Elymas, who opposes the true faith.
keyPoints: The church at Antioch fasts and prays, and the Holy Spirit instructs them to set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work.
At Paphos, they encounter the false prophet Barjesus; Paul rebukes his wickedness, and he is struck blind for a season.
At Antioch in Pisidia, Paul preaches in the synagogue that Jesus is the Savior, and many believe.
chapters.application: Today let us obey the Holy Spirit's leading and boldly proclaim the gospel, not shrinking back in the face of opposition, for the Lord will surely give us strength and bring many to turn to him.

chapters.summary: Paul and Barnabas preach in Iconium, Lystra, and other places, suffering persecution, but they persevere in the gospel and strengthen the faith of the disciples.
keyPoints: In Iconium they preach boldly, and though opposed, they still perform signs and wonders.
Stirred up by the Jews, Paul is stoned and left for dead, but he rises up and goes back into the city.
They strengthen the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and appoint elders.
chapters.application: Believers should follow Paul's example, boldly preaching the gospel even amid hardship, and strengthening the faith of others, understanding that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.

chapters.summary: The Jerusalem council decides that Gentile believers need not be circumcised, requiring only a few basic restrictions, and the church remains united as it sends messengers to convey the decision.
keyPoints: Paul and Barnabas go up to Jerusalem to discuss the question of circumcision with the apostles and elders.
Peter testifies that God has given the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles, and James cites the prophets in support of receiving them.
The church writes to the churches at Antioch and elsewhere, setting circumcision aside but asking believers to abstain from idols and from sexual immorality.
chapters.application: In the midst of disagreement, let us follow the example of the early church - seeking the Spirit's guidance, standing on Scripture and testimony, pursuing peace and unity, and not laying our own traditions upon others.

chapters.summary: On Paul's second missionary journey, Timotheus joins him; led by the Spirit into Macedonia, they establish a church at Philippi and even experience praise in prison.
keyPoints: Paul chooses Timotheus to accompany him and circumcises him for the sake of reaching the Jews.
The Holy Spirit forbids them to preach in Asia and instead leads them toward Macedonia in answer to a vision calling them there.
At Philippi, Lydia believes, Paul casts out a spirit of divination, an earthquake shakes the prison, and the jailer and his household are saved.
chapters.application: When circumstances seem to block our way, let us stay alert to the Spirit's leading, confident that God will open a door for the gospel. In hardship, praising the Lord with joy can become a blessing to others.

chapters.summary: Paul preaches at Thessalonica, Berea, and Athens, meeting very different responses, and at Athens proclaims the one true God and the resurrection.
keyPoints: At Thessalonica, Paul explains that Christ had to suffer and rise again; many believe, but the Jews grow jealous and stir up a riot.
The Bereans are more noble than the Thessalonians, receiving the word eagerly and searching the Scriptures daily, though Jews from Thessalonica come to stir up trouble there too.
At Athens, Paul sees a city full of idols and, on Mars' Hill, proclaims the Creator and the resurrection; some mock, while others believe.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us search the Scriptures with the humility of the Bereans, and, like Paul, boldly proclaim the gospel, giving glory to the Creator.

chapters.summary: Paul establishes a church at Corinth, then passes through Ephesus and other places on his way back to Antioch, while Apollos preaches boldly in Achaia.
keyPoints: Paul stays with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth, reasoning in the synagogue every sabbath to persuade both Jews and Greeks.
When the Jews resist and revile him, Paul shakes out his garment as a sign of his innocence and turns to the Gentiles, and the Lord encourages him in a vision.
While Gallio is proconsul, the Jews bring accusations against Paul, but Gallio refuses to hear the case, and the crowd beats Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue.
themes: The Gospel Turns to the Gentiles
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, the Lord has promised to be with us; let us simply go on boldly proclaiming the gospel, trusting him to keep us and to provide us with fellow workers.

chapters.summary: Paul preaches at Ephesus, where disciples of John's baptism receive the Holy Spirit and miracles take place, until a riot breaks out over the silver trade and is finally quieted.
keyPoints: Paul lays hands on the Ephesian believers, the Holy Spirit comes upon them, and they are baptized in the Spirit and speak in tongues.
Paul reasons daily in the school of Tyrannus, and God works extraordinary miracles through him, overpowering evil spirits.
Demetrius stirs up the silversmiths, throwing the whole city into confusion, until the town clerk calms the crowd.
chapters.application: As the gospel spreads, opposition is bound to arise. Let us depend on the Spirit, hold fast to the truth, and bear witness to peace even in conflict, trusting that the Lord will watch over his church.

chapters.summary: Paul concludes his ministry at Ephesus, encourages the Ephesian elders, warns them to watch carefully over the flock, and foretells that he himself will be bound.
keyPoints: At Troas, Paul preaches long into the night; Eutychus falls from the window, but God raises him back to life.
From Miletus, Paul sends for the elders of Ephesus and tells them of his own ministry and purpose.
Paul urges the elders to watch carefully over themselves and the whole flock, to shepherd the church of God, and to guard against savage wolves.
chapters.application: Wherever we find ourselves, let us keep Christ at the center, serve faithfully, uphold the weak, and remember the Lord's own words: it is more blessed to give than to receive.

chapters.summary: Against every warning, Paul resolutely sets out for Jerusalem, taking leave of the disciples along the way; on his arrival he joins in a temple rite, but is seized amid a Jewish uproar.
keyPoints: At Tyre and Caesarea, disciples and the prophet Agabus warn Paul that he will suffer in Jerusalem, but Paul remains resolved to lay down his life for the Lord.
Arriving in Jerusalem, Paul reports to James and the elders on the conversion of the Gentiles, and agrees to take part in a purification rite to ease the concerns of Jewish believers.
In the temple, Jews from Asia stir up the crowd against Paul, throwing the whole city into an uproar, until the Roman commander rescues him and binds him with chains.
themes: Courage in the Face of Persecution
chapters.application: When we face difficult decisions, may the Lord give us Paul's courage - to submit faithfully to God's will and be willing to pay the cost for the gospel.

chapters.summary: In Jerusalem, Paul recounts to the Jewish crowd his own conversion and speaks in his own defense, until his mention of the Gentiles throws the people into an uproar.
keyPoints: Paul addresses the people in Hebrew, explaining that he himself is a Jew, trained under Gamaliel.
He describes in detail his encounter with the Lord Jesus on the road to Damascus, and how Ananias laid hands on him and baptized him.
When Paul mentions that the Lord sent him to the Gentiles far away, the crowd grows furious and demands his death.
chapters.application: Whatever the circumstances, speak boldly of what God has done in your life, and remain faithful to proclaim the gospel without shrinking back because of how others may respond.

chapters.summary: Paul is put on trial before the council, escapes danger when the Pharisees and Sadducees fall into dispute, is comforted by the Lord in a vision, and is later escorted to Caesarea.
keyPoints: Paul defends himself before the council, and his mention of the resurrection of the dead sparks a dispute between the two factions.
The Lord appears to Paul by night, encouraging him that as he has testified in Jerusalem, so he must also testify in Rome.
The Jews plot to kill Paul, but his nephew learns of it, and the commander sends soldiers to escort Paul safely to Caesarea.
chapters.application: When we face danger and persecution, God grants wisdom and protection. Let us hold fast to our faith with courage, trusting that he will guide the road ahead of us.

chapters.summary: Paul stands trial before Felix, defends himself, and is left waiting for further judgment.
keyPoints: The Jewish leaders accuse Paul of being a troublemaker, but their evidence is insufficient.
Paul makes his defense before Felix, declaring that he serves God according to the true Way.
Felix delays judgment and keeps Paul in custody for two years, during which Paul has occasion to speak to him about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.
chapters.application: When we face false accusations, let us answer calmly as Paul did, trusting that God is in control of all things; and even while we wait, let us seize every chance to proclaim the gospel.

chapters.summary: Paul stands trial before Festus, and because of the accusations of the Jews, appeals to Caesar; Festus agrees to send him on to Rome.
keyPoints: Festus takes office as governor, and the Jewish leaders again bring accusations against Paul.
Paul defends himself before Festus, insisting he has offended neither against the law of the Jews nor against Caesar.
Seeking a just hearing, Paul appeals to Caesar, and Festus grants his appeal.
chapters.application: When we face injustice and persecution, let us follow Paul's example - defending ourselves with courage, while trusting in God's sovereignty, believing he will guide every step we take.

chapters.summary: Paul defends himself before King Agrippa, recounting his conversion and calling all who hear him to believe.
keyPoints: Paul explains that he lived strictly according to the Pharisees' teaching, hoping in the resurrection God had promised.
Paul testifies that he met the Lord on the road to Damascus and was called to preach the gospel to the Gentiles.
Paul stresses that what he preaches agrees with what the prophets and Moses foretold, and urges his hearers to repent and believe.
chapters.application: Like Paul, let us boldly testify to the Lord's grace in whatever circumstances we find ourselves, firmly believing that God's promises will be fulfilled.

chapters.summary: Paul sails for Rome, and on the way a violent storm nearly costs everyone their lives, but Paul declares in faith that God will preserve them, and at last all reach the island of Melita safely.
keyPoints: Paul, a prisoner, is sent toward Rome and faces danger throughout the voyage.
Paul warns that the ship will come to disaster, but the crew does not believe him, and the storm strikes just as he foretold.
Paul comforts everyone aboard, declaring that God has promised he will stand before Caesar and has granted him the lives of all who sail with him.
chapters.application: In the storms of life, let us trust God's promises; he will preserve us to the end and grant us peace and a way through.

chapters.summary: Paul lands at Rome, and though a prisoner, boldly proclaims the kingdom of God; the Jews respond in different ways, while the Gentiles receive salvation.
keyPoints: On the island of Melita, Paul is bitten by a venomous snake yet remains unharmed, showing God's protection.
In Rome, Paul speaks with the Jewish leaders, quoting Isaiah concerning Israel's hardened heart.
Paul rents a house in Rome and preaches boldly, unhindered by anyone, and the gospel reaches the heart of the empire.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, God protects us. Let us face challenges in faith and seize every chance to proclaim the gospel, for God's word will never fail.
